where: Figure and its caption (Section 3 add-drop description)
problem: The through output of the grating is labelled "Port 2". Circulator port 2 is the arm that feeds the grating, so the figure shows the same port name twice and teaches the wrong topology: it says λ1 and λ3 leave at port 2, while the text says they 'pass straight through to the output line'. A student would conclude the through channels come back out of circulator port 2.
fix: Label that node 'Output line (through)' with note 'λ1, λ3 continue'. Caption: 'Light entering port 1 of the circulator leaves at port 2 and reaches the grating. The grating reflects λ2 back into port 2, so the circulator sends it out at port 3 as the dropped channel; λ1 and λ3 pass through the grating to the output line.'

problem: 'Fused birefringent coupler' is not the standard name for the device described (two fibers fused and tapered). The description itself is correct, but the name will not match textbooks or exam keys.
fix: Call it the 'fused biconical taper (FBT) coupler', made by placing or twisting two single-mode fibers together, fusing and tapering (stretching) the joint.

problem: The side lobes are called 'small unwanted notches'. In a reflecting grating the side lobes are small unwanted reflection peaks just outside the main reflected band; calling them notches reverses the meaning and muddles the crosstalk explanation given later in Q6.
fix: 'A sharp start and stop produce side lobes: small unwanted reflection peaks just outside the main reflected band, sitting right on neighbouring WDM channels.'

problem: The symbols P3in and P1leak appear in the formula but are never defined, and the layout 'P3in' reads as P times 3in.
fix: Write: Directivity = 10 log₁₀(P₃,forward/P₁,leak) dB, where P₃,forward is the output at port 3 for light fed into port 1, and P₁,leak is the small power appearing at port 1 when light is fed into port 3.
